name: Human genome draft
summary: An international public consortium assembled and freely posted a working draft of the human genome in 2000, covering most of it though with gaps.
description: The public consortium’s assembled draft provided broad human genome sequence coverage while retaining gaps and ambiguities.
tier_reason: The genome reference resource supports subsequent genetic mapping, comparative biology and medical interpretation; rank concerns the shared dataset, not completeness of the first draft.

impact.note: One dataset that gave biomedical researchers genome-wide lookup and from which genomics grew; reach of one profession and generativity 2 imply tier 1, not reviewed tier 0.

market.note: Commercial availability is not a milestone of a scientific knowledge result.

date.label: Oct 2000
date.basis: Anchored to the 7 October 2000 data snapshot analysed in the February 2001 paper.

events.statement: The public consortium’s assembled draft provided broad human genome sequence coverage while retaining gaps and ambiguities.
events.caveats: Not a gapless genome, an inventory of every human variant, or proof that all reported gene-count interpretations remained correct.

date.label: by 6 July 2000
date.basis: The UCSC press release dated 6 July reports that the working draft was already posted. The time of initial access is not established; UCSC’s later history says 7 July.

events.statement: UCSC reported that its public-consortium working-draft human-genome assembly had been posted on the web by 6 July 2000.
events.caveats: The original UCSC press release says the draft was already posted on 6 July; the later UCSC project history dates the web release to 7 July. This is not a resolved exact first-access date. The July draft predates and differs from the version assembled from data available on 7 October 2000.

evidence.locator: 2013 reprint, original 6 July 2000 press-release heading and first paragraph
evidence.supports: The contemporaneous dated release says the working draft had already been posted and was searchable and downloadable.
A later UCSC project history instead dates the web release to 7 July; this conflicting account is retained.

date.basis: Date of the cited public report or documented event.

events.statement: The public consortium published its analysis of a draft based on map and sequence data available on 7 October 2000.
events.caveats: The report does not establish the first public access to this exact assembled version or universal acceptance; some underlying data were released earlier.

evidence.locator: pp. 860, 864–867; publication date on issue header
evidence.supports: Published report describes the freely available draft and identifies the data snapshot used for analysis.

links.statement: Mapped-clone sequencing and assembly generated the public human draft analysed from the October 2000 snapshot.
links.alternatives: Whole-genome shotgun was a contemporary alternative.
links.caveats: Multiple datasets and assembly decisions contributed.
links.timing: Production and resulting draft overlap; the endpoint is a snapshot, not a later all-gaps-closed milestone.
